symbols.name: transform length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in each input and output vector of the transform.
symbols.quote: Let $q$ be the length of the transform: the number of entries in each input and output vector.

symbols.name: input vector
symbols.meaning: The input vector of the transform, with entries $u_0$ through $u_{q-1}$.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be the input vector, with entries $u_0$ through $u_{q-1}$.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: An index into the input vector, an integer from 0 to q-1.
symbols.quote: Let $j$ be an input position and $k$ an output position, each an integer from $0$ to $q-1$.

symbols.name: output position
symbols.meaning: An index into the output vector, an integer from 0 to q-1.
symbols.quote: Let $j$ be an input position and $k$ an output position, each an integer from $0$ to $q-1$.

symbols.name: transform
symbols.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform of length q, normalized by 1/q.
symbols.quote: Write $F_q$ for this transform of the input vector.

symbols.name: coordinatewise product
symbols.meaning: The product of two vectors of length q taken entry by entry.
symbols.quote: The dot $\cdot$ denotes coordinatewise multiplication of two vectors of length $q$.

symbols.name: cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two vectors of length q.
symbols.quote: The star $\ast$ denotes cyclic convolution of two vectors $x$ and $y$ of length $q$.

symbols.name: first operand
symbols.meaning: The first of the two vectors of length q in the cyclic convolution.
symbols.quote: The star $\ast$ denotes cyclic convolution of two vectors $x$ and $y$ of length $q$.

symbols.name: second operand
symbols.meaning: The second of the two vectors of length q in the cyclic convolution.
symbols.quote: The star $\ast$ denotes cyclic convolution of two vectors $x$ and $y$ of length $q$.

symbols.name: chirp
symbols.meaning: The chirp vector, whose entry at each integer m is e^{\pi i m^2/q}.
symbols.quote: The chirp is the vector $a$ whose entry at each integer $m$ is $a_m = e^{\pi i m^2/q}$.

symbols.name: integer argument
symbols.meaning: The integer at which the chirp entry a_m is evaluated.
symbols.quote: The chirp is the vector $a$ whose entry at each integer $m$ is $a_m = e^{\pi i m^2/q}$.

relations.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) as a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) multiplied by chirp factors.
It reduces the transform to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so any method that computes that convolution also computes the transform.
